description:
Factory AI GMO's commercial platform needs a catalog of subscription plan tiers to render the public marketing Pricing page (docx section 8, 'Commercial Product Scope' — Pricing is listed as its own public-website surface, distinct from Billing/usage enforcement). This module does not sit on the milestones doc's stated authenticated dependency chain (Account -> Organization -> Projects -> Factory Runs -> Artifacts -> Usage -> Billing); it is the public-facing content behind that chain's 'plan' concept, not a step in it. `organization.plan` (tests/prd_organization.json) already stores a free-text plan tier per-Organization but explicitly leaves 'allowed values and their meaning... not prescribed here' — this module is the natural place those values and their public price/feature presentation would eventually live, but this PRD does not force that link (see Open Architectural Question #1).

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
- Unauthenticated visitors on the public marketing website can read the current list of published (isActive=true) pricing plans, in display order, to render the Pricing page.
- Authorized internal staff (see Open Architectural Question #2 on role vocabulary) can create, edit, publish/unpublish, and reorder plans.
- Each plan has a stable machine-readable code, a human-readable display name, a monthly price, an optional yearly price, a currency, a feature list, a call-to-action label and destination, a 'featured' flag for visual emphasis, a published flag, and a display order.
- Unpublished plans must never appear in the public read response, even though internal staff can still see and edit them.

CONSTRAINTS -- already decided, satisfy them rather than re-deciding them
- This is a commercial-platform, tenant-independent entity, following the same reasoning already established for factoryAccount (ADR-003) and organization: a pricing plan has no existing companyId relationship to POS GMO's own `companies` table, and must never be given a companyId -- it belongs to Factory AI GMO's own commercial product, not to a POS GMO retail tenant. State this plainly, not only in prose framing, per the lesson recorded in Milestone 2 (organization's first-draft classification gap).
- created_At and updated_at are server-controlled, same convention as every other module in this repository.
- Price fields are monetary: DECIMAL type, TIER_2_FINANCIAL convention (DECIMAL(10,2) storage, no float rounding in application code) -- same rule already enforced for every other financial module in this repository.
- The public read endpoint must return only isActive=true plans, ordered by sortOrder ascending, and must not expose any internal-only field (there are none sensitive here today, but the filter itself -- excluding unpublished plans -- is not optional).
- The public read endpoint accepts no write parameters; it is read-only. Creating, editing, publishing, or reordering plans requires internal authorization.

OPEN ARCHITECTURAL QUESTIONS -- deliberately unresolved; do not silently pick an answer and hide the ambiguity
1. Link to organization.plan: should planCode become the authoritative source of truth for the values organization.plan is allowed to hold (effectively a soft enum), or are the two intentionally decoupled (an Organization's billed plan vs. the public marketing catalog can diverge, e.g. grandfathered or custom enterprise deals)? Do not invent a formal FK from organization.plan to this table -- organization's own table is not confirmed live yet (see Milestone 2/3), and forcing a relationship here would hit the same invented-table guard project's PRD already exercised (gate_result.warnings). Decide and justify whichever relationship model is used, including 'intentionally none yet'.
2. Role vocabulary: who manages pricing content is an internal Factory AI GMO staff decision (product/finance ops), not a per-customer-Organization permission -- the same role-model mismatch already flagged as carried-forward and unresolved in organization's and project's PRDs (AllowedRole only offers Admin/Manager/Cashier, POS-retail-operations roles that don't fit this platform's actual staff model). roles_allowed below uses the closest available value only because the schema requires one; it is not a real access-model decision and should not be treated as one downstream.
3. Yearly price derivation: is priceYearly independently authored by staff, or should it be computed from priceMonthly (e.g. a fixed annual-discount percentage)? Not decided here -- do not invent a discount formula as a side effect of this PRD.
4. Currency/localization scope: is a single currency sufficient for v1, or must the public endpoint support multiple currencies/locales (query param, Accept-Language, geo-detection)? Not decided here -- do not invent an i18n mechanism.
5. Price-change / grandfathering policy: when a plan's price changes, what happens to Organizations already subscribed at the old price? This module only stores the current price; it does not version price history or model grandfathering. That belongs to Billing (not yet built, per the milestones doc's 'Next' section) -- do not invent versioning or grandfathering logic here, only note that current-price-only is what v1 stores.
6. Public marketing page generation itself: this PRD's frontend section covers only the internal Admin management UI (List + Detail, role-gated), following this repository's established frontend_agent pattern (CLAUDE.md: route guards, authenticated pages). The actual public, unauthenticated /pricing marketing page that unauthenticated visitors see is a different kind of surface than anything frontend_agent has been asked to generate elsewhere in this repository (every existing generated page sits behind a role guard; CLAUDE.md states public routes are '/login only'). Whether generating that public page is in scope for this factory at all, or whether it belongs to a separate marketing-site codebase that merely calls the public read endpoint below, is an open question this PRD deliberately does not resolve.

This PRD intentionally leaves schema shape, relationships, and endpoints beyond what's named above to the Architect/Database/Backend agents to determine, consistent with the commercialization plan's own instruction that the exact modules and schema should be discovered and designed by the Software Factory from the commercial requirements, not assumed in advance.

fields.name: planCode
fields.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for this plan, e.g. 'free', 'pro', 'enterprise' -- distinct from the human-readable planName. Whether this becomes the authoritative value-set for organization.plan (tests/prd_organization.json) is Open Architectural Question #1, not decided here.

fields.name: planName
fields.description: Human-readable plan name shown on the pricing page, e.g. 'Pro'.

fields.name: tagline
fields.description: Short marketing subtitle shown under the plan name, e.g. 'For growing teams'.

fields.name: priceMonthly
fields.description: Monthly price. DECIMAL storage (TIER_2_FINANCIAL convention), no float rounding in application code.

fields.name: priceYearly
fields.description: Optional yearly price. Whether it is independently authored or derived from priceMonthly is Open Design Question #3 -- not decided here.

fields.name: currency
fields.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD. Whether multi-currency/locale support is required is Open Design Question #4 -- not decided here.

fields.name: featuresList
fields.description: Feature bullets shown on this plan's pricing card. Exact structure (delimited text vs. JSON array) is left to the Architect/Backend agents to decide, not prescribed here.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.description: Call-to-action button label, e.g. 'Start free trial', 'Contact sales'.

fields.name: ctaUrl
fields.description: Destination for the CTA button, e.g. a signup route or a leadCapture-sourced contact path (tests/prd_leadCapture.json). This PRD does not require that link be wired to leadCapture specifically -- open, not decided here.

fields.name: isFeatured
fields.description: Highlights this plan as the recommended/most-popular option on the pricing page. Whether more than one plan may be featured at once, and how that's enforced, is an open design question.

fields.name: isActive
fields.description: Whether this plan is currently published on the public pricing page. Defaults to true. Plans with isActive=false must never be returned by the public read endpoint.

fields.name: sortOrder
fields.description: Display order on the pricing page, ascending. Tie-breaking when two plans share a sortOrder, and reordering mechanics, are an open design question, the same category of question left open for leadCapture's and organization's ordering/lifecycle fields.

components.name: PricingPlanListStep
components.description: IonList of all plans (published and unpublished), showing planName, priceMonthly, isFeatured/isActive badges, and sortOrder with reordering controls.

components.name: PricingPlanDetailPage
components.description: Create/edit form at /admin/pricing-plans/:id for a single plan's fields, including publish/unpublish and featured toggles.

endpoints.description: Public, unauthenticated endpoint that returns only isActive=true plans, ordered by sortOrder ascending, for the marketing site's Pricing page to render. Accepts no write parameters. Must not expose any field that isn't meant for public display. Error responses must not leak internal implementation details.
